PullRequest.Title: Show structural changes in the Source Control Graph view
PullRequest.Body:

While the Source Control view shows structural changes, the files of the history items in the Source Control Graph view now expand to the symbols that changed in them, like the files in the Source Control view and in the file list of the multi-file diff editor (#350138). The Graph view reuses the structural diff model and renderer that #350137 made reusable. The providers need no change: they already analyze the `git:` documents of a history item, which the multi-file diff editor shows as well.

### Change

- **Expanding files:** a file of a history item that a structural diff provider supports can expand to its changed symbols. Like in the Source Control view, files are collapsed until the user expands them, and expand through their twistie, since clicking them opens them; a double-click also toggles them, which a follow-up will change in all structural diff views. They load their symbols when expanded, and keep none when collapsed or while the view is hidden. Added and deleted files can't expand, since a structural diff needs both versions.
- **Toggle:** like the file list of the multi-file diff editor, the Graph view follows the Source Control view's Show Structural Diff, that is the `scm.structuralDiff.enabled` setting and the choice of the workspace. Turning it off moves the focus and selection from symbols to their files.
- **Rendering:** symbol rows reuse the Source Control view's renderer and continue the lanes of the graph. Their status letters end where those of the files end. In a list, all files keep their twistie space while files can expand; in a tree, files follow the Explorer, like in the Source Control view.
- **Opening a symbol** opens the diff of its file in the history item, with the same title as opening the file, and selects the symbol. The new `openStructuralDiff` takes the diff to open; the Source Control view's `openSCMStructuralDiff` uses it.
- **Refresh and Load More:** both create the history items of the graph again. A file keeps its element while its history item is in the graph and the file compares the same documents, and the element takes the graph data of the new history item. So an expanded file keeps its symbols without being analyzed again, also below a folder that was collapsed during a refresh, and a refresh doesn't wait for symbols that are already loaded. Like in the Source Control view, a refresh waits for symbols that are still loading. After each update, the files of history items that the graph no longer shows are forgotten, and the symbols of files that it doesn't show expanded are released, also when switching between list and tree shows an expanded file again, collapsed.
- **Telemetry:** `scmStructuralDiffRequested` reports the new location `scmGraph`. The model's `releaseWhere` now ends the expansion of the files that it releases, like `release`, so expanding a file again that the graph showed collapsed is reported, while reloads of expanded files still aren't. The model only knows the files with structural changes, so `releaseWhere` also takes the files that a view reuses, and the Graph passes the files it keeps. This also covers files whose structural changes were cleared, for example by hiding the view or a provider change.
- The description of the setting, the accessibility help of the Graph view and the documentation of `ISCMViewService` mention the Graph view.

### Testing

- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/browser/scmHistoryViewPane.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/browser/scmStructuralDiff.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/test/common/scmStructuralDiff.test.ts`: passed (101 tests). New tests check that the data source keeps the element of a file across a refresh in list and tree mode and gives it the new graph data, but creates a new element when the file compares other documents or its history item left the graph; that files have structural children only while structural diffs are enabled; and that the accessibility help of the Graph view describes structural changes only while they are available. Tests with a tree like the Graph view's check that a file below a folder that was collapsed during a refresh keeps its element and isn't analyzed again on the next refresh, and that switching between list and tree in both directions releases the symbols of an expanded file that it shows collapsed, but keeps its element. Those three fail with the first commit's cleanup, which forgot and released only the files that the tree no longer showed, and the reuse tests fail when the data source doesn't reuse elements. The reporting test of the model also checks that a file released through `releaseWhere` reports its next expansion, which fails without the change of `releaseWhere`. Another model test checks that a view ends the expansion of a reused file without results only when it releases the file. A Graph test checks that a nested file that showing the view drops from a collapsed folder, after hiding the view cleared its structural changes, reports its next expansion, while a file that stays expanded doesn't. Both fail when the reused files aren't passed.
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js` with the same three files and `--browser webkit --browser chromium`: passed (100 tests in each browser; the Electron run also counts the runner's registry check).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run valid-layers-check` and `pnpm run check-cyclic-dependencies`: passed.
- On the changed files, `node build/oxlint.ts`, `node --experimental-strip-types build/lib/formatter.ts --verify`, `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts` and `node build/stylelint.ts` (for `scm.css`): passed.
- Manually in Code OSS with a test provider and a repository whose graph has two lanes: list and tree mode, symbol rows next to both lanes with the status letters of symbols and files aligned, refresh and Load More without new provider requests, collapsing and expanding a file, opening a symbol with Enter, and turning the setting off and on.

To test manually: with `scm.structuralDiff.enabled`, expand a history item in the Source Control Graph view and then a TypeScript file that it modified. The file lists its changed symbols, and Enter on a symbol opens the diff of the file at that symbol.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new subscription and undefined-change handler reach a recursive root update. AsyncDataTree refreshes expanded history items concurrently, and the traced Git provider executes an uncached diff for each one. The view-model and element caches do not bypass those calls. Duration and prevalence of large expanded commits are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Extension-host IPC calls, git diff subprocesses, and repeated full commit-change payloads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N expanded history items, each completed structural-only root update issues N history-change IPC requests and normally N git diff subprocesses, not one call per file. AsyncDataTree runs these sibling requests concurrently; the structural model's three-load limiter does not constrain them. Work also grows with the files and rename detection in each commit.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary subprocess/I/O bursts and payload allocation delay graph rendering and subsequent operations queued on the tree sequencer.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Changing Show Structural Diff or an unrelated document's language did not re-query the graph's expanded commits. History change queries occurred when expanding commits or explicitly refreshing/updating the graph.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: An undefined structural-model notification now recursively refreshes the graph root, including all expanded history items, even when no file has been expanded for structural changes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added onDidChange subscription at line 2298 routes structural model notifications to this newly added _updateChildren() call at line 2515. Before this diff, structural enablement/provider/language changes had no subscription that refreshed the graph.
Findings.Title: Refresh file nodes without re-querying every expanded commit
Findings.Impact: With several commits expanded, toggling Show Structural Diff, registering a structural provider, or changing even an unrelated editor's language re-runs each commit's Git diff. Large commits can make the graph update slow and hold up a subsequent Refresh or Load More, despite unchanged history and warm structural results.
Findings.Evidence: StructuralDiffModel.setEnabled and its provider/language listeners emit undefined (common/scmStructuralDiff.ts:307-329, 335-345). The new handler calls _updateChildren, which queues recursive tree.updateChildren at scmHistoryViewPane.ts:2480-2490. AsyncDataTree.doRefreshSubTree refreshes siblings via Promises.settled and setChildren includes expanded children (asyncDataTree.ts:1132-1137, 1270-1290). Each expanded history item calls provideHistoryItemChanges at scmHistoryViewPane.ts:1157 before consulting _getChangeElements. MainThreadSCM crosses IPC at mainThreadSCM.ts:255-262. GitHistoryProvider immediately calls repository.diffBetweenWithStats (extensions/git/src/historyProvider.ts:340-345), reaching an uncached git diff --raw --numstat --find-renames invocation (extensions/git/src/git.ts:1965-1980). getHistoryItems caches only history view models, not these change requests.
Findings.Recommendation: Handle structural-only notifications by updating the existing file nodes' expandability and structural children, without refreshing their history-item ancestors. Keep full graph/history queries for actual history refreshes and pagination.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the graph and expand history items, with structural files initially collapsed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial rendering waits for repository initialization, history/filter resolution and setInput. Expanding a history item waits for its complete change list. Structural document loading does not run merely because its files are listed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve history refs/common ancestor and retrieve a page through extension-host IPC and Git log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One history request per page (page size clamped to 1..1000), plus applicable ref/common-ancestor requests; not one log per commit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same history/filter/page requests existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the initial graph/page can render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Optional GitHub assignable-user and commit-author queries used by the existing history details provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold: one assignable-user query per uncached owner/repository, then one commit-author query per remaining author group after user-cache, incomplete-commit and no-reply-email checks. Warm successful groups avoid requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical page-level grouping, repository cache and optional network behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing history provider awaits avatar resolution before returning its page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve one commit's changes via IPC and git diff --raw --numstat with rename detection; deserialize its URI payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one history-change IPC and one Git diff per expanded history item; special incoming/outgoing comparisons also resolve an ancestor. The result serves all files in that item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commit-level query was required before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Expansion waits for the change list.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: H loaded history items, N expanded history items, and the sum of their changed-file counts. Avatar fan-out uses distinct uncached author groups, not commits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tree operations are sequenced; recursive sibling history-item requests can run concurrently. Initial page retrieval is awaited. GitHub assignable-user loading is sequentialized, while author-group requests use Promise.all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: History view models are cached until refresh/pagination invalidates or extends them. Commit-change queries are not cached. New file-element maps preserve object identity but are populated only after the history-change request; structural results are absent while files remain collapsed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: default collapse behavior, tree refresh logic, provider implementations and model guards were read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size, rename cost, authentication and remote latency vary. These existing boundaries are not independently findings.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new eager file-content/provider work on ordinary graph opening. Required existing history requests remain grouped per history item/page.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicitly expand supported modified files to show structural symbols
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Expansion waits for a load slot, both document references, worker text diff, and a successful structural provider or cached failure/status. Added/deleted files without both versions cannot start structural loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve git document models, stat their objects and read contents through the extension filesystem provider using Git ls-tree and show --textconv.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two distinct document URIs per file before URI-level reference coalescing. A cold successful ordinary git document read entails a stat and content read, normally one ls-tree and one show; existing referenced models avoid reloading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The graph had no file-to-symbol expansion, so listing commit files did not resolve these documents. Opening their file diffs already used the document-loading boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both model resolutions must settle before structural computation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize models and compute a text diff in the worker, then request structural interpretation from the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker diff per uncached file entry; structural providers are tried sequentially in selector order until one succeeds. Full document synchronization is keyed by URI/model lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No symbol computation in the graph; this same reusable computation was already used in other structural-diff surfaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the requested symbol result; worker computation and overall loading have time budgets.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F explicitly expanded supported files; D distinct document URIs after coalescing, D <= 2F; document sizes and returned symbol/text-change counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single graph StructuralDiffModel limits loads to three; both documents within each load resolve concurrently. Providers within a file are sequential. Cancellation frees a load slot, although already-issued document I/O may finish later and is disposed on arrival.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An entry keyed by stable file-element identity coalesces pending requests and caches success, empty results and failure/status. URI-level model references coalesce shared documents. Content/provider/language changes invalidate as appropriate; file collapse/hiding releases entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lazy expansion, entry.pending joining, load limiter, model reference collection, filesystem implementation and provider RPC were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Document sizes and extension provider computation vary; no runtime measurements. Outstanding non-cancelable I/O can outlive a slot, an existing model behavior rather than a new independent mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: New expensive work is explicitly requested and bounded/coalesced using the existing model. No high-confidence avoidable regression on normal expansion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh, Load More, or change list/tree presentation while symbols are expanded
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The queued root update waits for any required history/page queries, all refreshed expanded history-item change lists, and outstanding structural loads before rendering. Cleanup follows the completed update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch a new history page on Load More or refreshed history on Refresh, and retrieve change lists for expanded history items.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One history request per required page; normally N change-list IPC/Git diff calls for N expanded history items. Warm presentation-only updates skip log retrieval but not existing change-list queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Root updates already refreshed expanded commit change lists and pagination/history queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The root update waits for the sibling requests before rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload structural data only for still-expanded file entries whose results are missing; join pending work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero extra provider/model loads for warm unchanged retained elements. Changed document pairs or previously released expanded entries miss; already-pending requests are joined, not issued twice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There were no graph symbol children to refresh or await.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pending/missing structural results now participate in the recursive update, as required by the async tree; completed cached results settle immediately.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N expanded history items, F retained file elements, and expanded supported files with cache misses; pagination grows the loaded history collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Root operations are throttled and sequenced. Expanded sibling history items run concurrently. Structural misses share the three-load limiter; in-flight results coalesce. Pending disposal settles tree waits promptly.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: File identity is preserved when history identity and original/modified URIs match. Recreated history view models update the element's graph data. Files below collapsed folders retain reusable identity, but absent/collapsed file results are released after updates. History items absent from the tree are removed from the element map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete diff, cache reuse tests and async tree identity/collapse behavior establish warm reuse and cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold provider latency can extend a refresh; this intentional async-tree ordering is explicit and bounded, not a demonstrated additional avoidable regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No duplicate warm symbol analysis was found. Existing history-query multiplicity is unchanged for these actual graph updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle Show Structural Diff or receive provider/language notifications while the graph has expanded commits
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new undefined-change handler queues a recursive root refresh. Rendering and later sequenced graph operations wait for every expanded commit's change query even when history is unchanged and no structural file is expanded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-request full change lists and run Git diff with stats/rename detection for every expanded history item on a structural-only notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally N change IPC requests and N Git diff subprocesses per completed root update, for N expanded history items. Each serves a whole commit, not an individual file. The root history-page cache does not reduce these N calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These structural-only events did not refresh the graph or issue graph history-change queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All sibling change requests must finish before the graph rerenders; they also occupy the shared tree-operation sequencer ahead of Refresh/Load More.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recompute expanded symbols when provider changes invalidate entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Provider changes can additionally reload F expanded supported files, limited to three loads. An unrelated model-language change can retain all structural results yet still cause the N history queries above. Disabling clears results immediately and still triggers those history queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No structural children in this graph; no graph notification subscriber.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required structural invalidation work is awaited alongside avoidable history queries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N expanded history items (realistically multiple commits left expanded while browsing), their total changed-file counts and rename workloads, and the number of completed structural-triggered updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The throttler coalesces queued root work but does not debounce all notifications into a single future update. Each root operation is sequenced, with N sibling history queries concurrently issued; Git run/exec do not impose a shared limiter here. The three-load structural limiter applies only to symbol loads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm getHistoryItems returns cached view models. _getChangeElements and structural entries preserve identities/results but run only after provideHistoryItemChanges, so neither prevents the repeated Git/IPC queries. No history-change positive or in-flight cache exists on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event sources, added subscription/handler, recursive expanded-child selection, IPC proxy and uncached spawning path all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of notifications and costly commits is unmeasured; the feature is experimental/opt-in. This lowers severity, not confidence in the added fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity boundary-fanout regression at added line 2515. Structural-only updates should operate on existing file nodes instead of their history ancestors.

Scenarios.Scenario: Collapse files, hide/show the graph, switch presentation, or remove history items
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Collapsing a file or hiding the view immediately disposes its structural entries and settles pending waits. Showing the view reconstructs its input; root-update cleanup removes results no longer represented by expanded file nodes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel computations and dispose held model references; re-resolve documents only if the user subsequently requests an uncached expansion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cleanup once per released entry; late already-issued model resolutions are disposed on arrival. Re-expansion can reload up to two distinct document models per file, subject to URI-level sharing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The graph retained no structural model references; the reusable disposal mechanism already existed for other structural-diff views.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Disposal settles the tree's entry wait without requiring underlying I/O completion. Reload is on subsequent expansion/showing, not background hidden-view analysis.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Currently retained/expanded files and visited files of history items still represented by the graph; no symbol result is generated for every loaded commit by default.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Disposal is immediate and cancels pending model computations; document loading already across a boundary can complete later. Reopening uses the same sequencer and three-load limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Hidden structural models clear results/references and refuse loading. File collapse ends expansion; absent/collapsed file entries are released after root updates. Reuse maps retain lightweight identity for represented history items and drop absent history items. Collapsed ancestors can preserve existing expanded descendants until a tree update; no separate unbounded document leak was established.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership in registered disposables, entry disposal races, releaseHiddenChanges and hide/show tests were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Element/symbol counts and hidden-tree retention depend on browsing history. Identity retention is intentional; no high-confidence independent catastrophic or unbounded regression was proven.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable cleanup/cache regression. The shared WeakSet deletion change affects telemetry expansion tracking, not strong memory ownership or expensive request multiplicity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll/render symbol rows and open a symbol's file diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Scrolling renders virtualized rows synchronously. Opening a symbol awaits one editor-open operation and selects the symbol only while its model generation remains current.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build row labels, hover registrations and an SVG lane placeholder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One render per virtualized visible/recycled symbol row, with one SVG path per graph lane; not DOM construction for the entire history collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Symbol rows did not exist; file rows already used the same lane-placeholder work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous row rendering; changed CSS adds flex/positioning without geometry reads or forced-layout mechanisms.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the existing file diff through the editor service and resolve documents if not already held by the editor/model collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One editor-open request per symbol activation, with at most the existing original/modified document pair; referenced document models are reused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Activating the file already opened the same document pair. The shared SCM opener is refactored without adding another open/load call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Editor opening must complete before symbol selection/reveal; there is no extra history query in this path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: V rendered rows, L graph lanes, and user activation frequency; document sizes only on model cache misses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering runs on the UI thread without new synchronous layout reads. Editor opening is awaited per activation; no collection-wide opening loop is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Virtualized templates reuse row widgets and clear element hover disposables when recycled. Symbol opening reuses existing model references and generation checks; no new content/result cache is introduced by the opener refactor.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderer delegation, template disposal, SVG implementation and before/after editor-input extraction were read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very wide graphs or unusually dense symbol results may increase normal rendering cost; no evidence establishes avoidable diff-introduced jank beyond the requested new rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence rendering or opener regression. Richer title/input metadata does not independently amplify expensive work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 10-file inventory and all diff pages in one performance-review pass. Traced graph initialization, expansion, refresh/pagination, structural notifications, cleanup, rendering, and editor opening. Submitted one high-confidence finding: structural-only notifications unnecessarily fan out into uncached history-change IPC/Git requests for every expanded history item. Identity reuse and cleanup otherwise preserve bounded, lazy structural loading. No concrete pre-existing performance regression fix qualifies for blame/provenance reporting. Static analysis; timings were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
